a00991e3d7.q: Why do couples struggle to spend more in retirement even when their financial plan shows they have enough money?
a00991e3d7.a: There is inherent discomfort in switching from working and accumulating wealth to spending. There is often fear of running out of money even when the numbers look good, and this fear is not always rational. If someone has been the cautious one in the relationship, they tend to continue being cautious even when everyone says it's okay to spend, especially if they are naturally risk averse.

f530bfb1b3.q: What is the first step couples should take when they have conflicting visions about retirement spending and money priorities?
f530bfb1b3.a: The first step is understanding each other. Each partner needs to acknowledge what the other person is needing and move closer to that. It is not one partner's job to get the other to do things their way. Couples need to recognize that their partners are coming from a good place, trying to achieve shared dreams, and then figure out how to give each other some version of what you're each wanting in retirement.

42d41b1998.q: How should someone approach rediscovering their identity and purpose after retiring from a career that defined their self-worth for decades?
42d41b1998.a: Rather than making an abrupt shift all at once, try establishing the things you want to do in retirement gradually before you retire. If you want to volunteer, start volunteering one afternoon a week and build connections. If you want to spend more time with grandkids, gradually increase that time rather than suddenly being available all the time. This helps with the transition so it is not like flipping a switch from working to retired.

749a7eee26.q: What are signs that someone has an unhealthy attachment to their job that will make retirement transition difficult?
749a7eee26.a: If a good majority of your time is spent doing or thinking about your work and you do not have a good balance with time spent with family and other activities, that can indicate an unhealthy attachment. Being a workaholic and putting all time and energy and money into work are signs. Additionally, if you have been in a career for a long time and have mastery of that role, you may not know how to be retired and spend extended time with your spouse.

2eea43e6cf.q: How long does it typically take for someone to shift their mindset from saving to spending in retirement?
2eea43e6cf.a: There is no fixed timeline, but the shift takes time. Rather than expecting a complete 180-degree change from saving to spending, a gradual approach works better. The recommendation is to do little gradual experiments of spending on things and seeing how you feel about it, allowing someone to become more comfortable as they do more rather than making an abrupt change.
